items.definition:
a river, canal, or other route for travel by water
The city is connected by a network of waterways.

a person employed to protect someone from harm
The celebrity arrived with a team of bodyguards.

a person who borrows something, especially money from a bank
The bank assesses the creditworthiness of each borrower.

noisy talk or conversation
The constant chatter in the classroom made it hard to concentrate.

a large American wild cat with a tawny coat, found from Canada to Patagonia
A cougar was spotted near the hiking trail.

the same thing again; aforesaid
She said she was tired, and I said ditto.

a small, thin piece of something
A snowflake is a tiny flake of ice.

a shallow trough fixed beneath the edge of a roof
Leaves often clog the rain gutter.

the sloping side of a hill
The sheep grazed peacefully on the hillside.

a type of cabbage with green or purple leaves
She added some fresh kale to her smoothie.

bad luck
It was a great misfortune that they lost everything.

a residential institution for the care and education of orphans
The children were raised in an orphanage after their parents died.

a thick, slippery, viscous substance
The snail left a trail of slime behind it.

a ballroom dance
They danced a beautiful waltz.

the operation or functioning
The working of the engine is very smooth.

a market in Middle Eastern countries
We bought souvenirs at the local bazaar.

a person who rides a bicycle or motorcycle
A group of bikers rode past.

the place where someone was born
This town is my birthplace.

a small book or magazine containing pictures and information
I picked up a brochure about the museum.

the stage of human social and cultural development and organization that is considered most advanced.
Ancient Egypt was a highly advanced civilisation.

a regulation requiring people to remain indoors between specified hours.
The city imposed a curfew after the protests.

a mound or ridge of sand or other loose sediment formed by the wind.
We walked over the sand dunes to reach the beach.

estimated time of arrival
What's your ETA?

a carnivorous mammal that lives in or near water
We saw an otter swimming in the river.

the part of a road used by vehicles
The roadway was wet and slippery after the rain.

a predatory arachnid with a segmented tail ending in a venomous sting
Be careful; there might be a scorpion under that rock.

a woody plant smaller than a tree, typically with multiple stems
The garden was full of flowering shrubs.

an official who watches a game or match closely to ensure that the rules are adhered to
The umpire made a controversial call.

a tool for gripping and turning nuts or bolts; a sudden, violent twist or pull
He used a wrench to tighten the bolt.

a light hit or a style of jazz
He gave the ball a gentle bop.

carbohydrate (informal)
I'm trying to cut down on carbs.

a layer of a substance covering a surface
The candy had a sugar coating.

a wild dog native to North America
We heard a coyote howling in the distance.

A type of deciduous tree.
The old elm tree stood tall in the park.

The woolly covering of a sheep or similar animal; a soft warm fabric.
She wore a warm fleece jacket.

A light, silly, or nervous laugh.
We heard a little giggle from the next room.

A rounded protuberance on the back of a camel or other animal, or on a person's back.
The camel has two humps on its back.

An act of interrupting or being interrupted.
We had a brief interruption during the meeting.

Land covered with grass and other low plants suitable for grazing animals
The cows grazed peacefully in the green pasture.

a cold-blooded vertebrate of a class that includes snakes, lizards, crocodiles, turtles, and tortoises
Snakes are a type of reptile.

a native or inhabitant of Spain
My friend is a Spaniard.

a boat or ship powered by steam; a cooking pot with a perforated bottom
We cooked the vegetables in a steamer.

the area next to a bed
She kept a glass of water on her bedside table.

a hat, typically one tied under the chin and worn by babies or women in the past; the hood of a car (British English)
She wore a straw bonnet to protect herself from the sun.

a type of fish with prominent barbels around the mouth
He caught a large catfish in the river.

a shop selling ready-to-eat food products
Let's grab a sandwich at the deli.

land used for farming
The region is known for its rich farmland.

spectacles worn to protect the eyes from glare, dust, water, etc.
He put on his swimming goggles before diving into the pool.

a person who plays golf
The golfer hit the ball straight down the fairway.

a native or inhabitant of Haiti, or a person of Haitian descent
Many Haitians live in the diaspora.

a woman who receives or entertains guests
The hostess greeted us warmly at the restaurant entrance.

a large mass of ice floating in the sea
Only the tip of the iceberg was visible above the water.

a wide road, often with trees or landscaping
We drove along the scenic parkway.

a small hard seed in a fruit; a spot on a playing card or dice
Don't swallow the apple pips.

a series of short, sharp, knocking sounds; a baby's toy
The baby played with its rattle.

a shorter or quicker way to get somewhere or do something
We took a shortcut through the park.

the action of an aircraft leaving the ground
The plane's takeoff was delayed due to fog.

exercise machine for walking or running
I run on the treadmill every morning.

a stinging insect
A wasp stung me on the arm.

a word naming an attribute of a noun
An adjective describes a noun.

a common pain-relieving drug
I took an aspirin for my headache.

a tool used for chopping wood, typically with a steel blade and a long wooden handle
He used an ax to chop the firewood.

A type of jacket, often worn as part of a uniform or for smart casual wear.
He wore a smart navy blazer to the interview.

A house built all on one level, without stairs.
They decided to buy a bungalow for their retirement.
